_doc: Per-skill misconception authoring template. Per ADR 0008: one JSON file per skill, named <skills.code>.json, lives under backend/seed/misconceptions/. The encoder projects the canonical five fields {id, label, description, contradicts_principle, distinguishing_mcq_stem} into skills.common_misconceptions JSONB and emits a versioned UPDATE migration. The encoder also injects an explicit label_ar: null per bac-curriculum rule 5 in ADR 0008. The seed file itself omits label_ar — the FR-only authoring path stays clean. schema_version 2 (per ADR 0009): distinguishing_mcq_stem is a structured object with five sub-keys — step 3 (distractor tagging) reads distractor_choice_label programmatically.

misconceptions.label: « La limite d'une somme est la somme des limites, même quand les limites individuelles n'existent pas »
misconceptions.description: L'élève applique le théorème de la somme — lim(f+g) = lim f + lim g — sans vérifier la condition d'existence : chaque limite individuelle doit exister (être finie ou infinie d'un signe déterminé). Face à lim(x→+∞) (x − sin(x)), il tente de décomposer en lim x + lim(−sin(x)), constate que sin(x) n'a pas de limite en +∞, puis conclut soit que la somme n'a pas de limite, soit qu'elle vaut +∞ « par défaut ». Le modèle erroné est que le théorème opératoire est une identité algébrique inconditionnelle, non une règle avec une prémisse.
misconceptions.contradicts_principle: Le théorème de la limite d'une somme est soumis à une condition d'existence : les deux limites individuelles doivent exister (finies ou infinies d'un signe déterminé) pour que l'on puisse conclure. L'absence de limite d'un terme ne transfère pas automatiquement à la somme — la somme peut avoir une limite même si un terme seul n'en a pas (cas où les oscillations se compensent ou où le terme dominant l'emporte structurellement).
evidence: Cornu (1991) — Limits, in Advanced Mathematical Thinking, Tall ed., pp.153–166 ; l'application inconditionnelle des théorèmes opératoires est l'un des obstacles de procédurisation les plus fréquents

Cadre de référence SM-A 2006 — unité « Limites et continuité » ; les théorèmes opératoires sont formulés avec les conditions d'existence explicites ; la distinction « théorème valide sous conditions » vs « identité algébrique » est un objectif explicite
Bac SMA session normale 2019, exercice sur les suites — forme lim(u_n + v_n) avec v_n oscillante ; l'erreur de décomposition sans condition y est diagnostiquée dans le corrigé

Bac SMA session de remplacement 2021, calcul de lim(x→+∞) (x + cos(x)) — le corrigé signale explicitement que cos(x) n'a pas de limite mais que le théorème de comparaison (et non le théorème additif) est la voie correcte

distinguishing_mcq_stem.stem_text: Soit f(x) = x + cos(x). Que peut-on dire de lim(x→+∞) f(x) ?  Choix : A) La limite n'existe pas car lim(x→+∞) cos(x) n'existe pas. ; B) lim(x→+∞) f(x) = +∞. ; C) lim(x→+∞) f(x) = 1 car cos(x) → 0 à l'infini. ; D) lim(x→+∞) f(x) = +∞ + lim cos(x), ce qui est indéfini.
distinguishing_mcq_stem.distractor_rationale: L'élève portant ce modèle décompose lim(x + cos x) = lim x + lim cos(x), constate que lim cos(x) n'existe pas, et conclut immédiatement que la somme n'a pas de limite — le théorème est appliqué à l'envers comme une condition nécessaire sans recours à un autre outil (théorème de comparaison). La démarche A est la signature exacte du modèle : l'inexistence d'un terme empêche la conclusion sur la somme.
distinguishing_mcq_stem.correct_rationale: Pour tout x, x − 1 ≤ x + cos(x) ≤ x + 1. Comme lim(x→+∞)(x − 1) = +∞, le théorème de comparaison (gendarmes en version minorante) donne lim(x→+∞)(x + cos x) = +∞, sans requérir l'existence de lim cos(x).

misconceptions.label: « lim f/g = lim f / lim g même quand lim g = 0 »
misconceptions.description: L'élève applique le théorème du quotient — lim(f/g) = lim f / lim g — sans vérifier que la limite du dénominateur est non nulle. Face à lim(x→1) (2x−1)/(x−1), il calcule lim(2x−1) = 1 et lim(x−1) = 0, puis effectue la division 1/0 et conclut soit que la limite est ∞, soit qu'elle n'existe pas, sans reconnaître que la forme 0/0 indéterminée requiert d'abord une factorisation. Variante : lim(x→0) sin(x)/x² — l'élève calcule 0/0, l'interprète comme 0 ou ∞ directement.
misconceptions.contradicts_principle: Le théorème du quotient lim(f/g) = lim f / lim g n'est valide que si lim g ≠ 0. Quand lim g = 0 et lim f ≠ 0, la limite est infinie (signe à déterminer par analyse de signe au voisinage). Quand lim g = 0 ET lim f = 0, la forme est indéterminée 0/0 et requiert une levée par factorisation, conjugué, ou équivalents — le théorème du quotient est inapplicable en l'état.
evidence: Tall & Vinner (1981) — Concept image and concept definition in mathematics, Educational Studies in Mathematics 12:151–169 ; l'image-concept du quotient comme opération algébrique inconditionnelle est l'une des causes d'erreur sur les formes indéterminées

Williams (1991) — Models of limit held by college calculus students, JRME 22(3):219–236 ; les étudiants appliquent les théorèmes opératoires mécaniquement sans vérifier les conditions ; le cas du dénominateur nul est le plus cité

Cadre de référence SM-A 2006 — la condition lim g ≠ 0 pour le théorème du quotient est formulée explicitement ; les cas lim g = 0 avec lim f ≠ 0 (limite infinie) et lim g = 0 avec lim f = 0 (forme indéterminée) sont distingués comme deux sous-cas à traiter différemment
Bac SMA session normale 2023, exercice 2 — lim(x→1) (x²−1)/(x−1) ; forme 0/0 ; le corrigé insiste sur l'inapplicabilité directe du théorème du quotient et la nécessité de la factorisation

distinguishing_mcq_stem.stem_text: lim(x→1) (x + 2) / (x − 1)² = ?  Choix : A) +∞ ; B) La limite n'existe pas car on divise par 0. ; C) −∞ ; D) 0.
distinguishing_mcq_stem.distractor_rationale: L'élève portant ce modèle calcule lim(x→1)(x+2) = 3, lim(x→1)(x−1)² = 0, applique mécaniquement le théorème du quotient à la forme 3/0, et conclut « on divise par 0 donc la limite n'existe pas » sans procéder à l'analyse de signe du dénominateur (l'étape précisément omise par le modèle erroné). La réponse B est la signature exacte de l'application de lim(f/g) = lim f / lim g sans vérification de la condition lim g ≠ 0, avec arrêt immédiat dès l'apparition de la forme c/0. Le stem est délibérément choisi en sous-cas 1/0 (et non 0/0) : 0/0 appartient au territoire de sma_limit_calc.M1 (forme-indéterminée-valeur-nulle), dont le raisonnement (« 0/0 = 0 ou indéfini ») pollue les distracteurs « doesn't exist » et « 0 » de manière dual-attribuable. Le cas 1/0 est, conformément au cadre SM-A, le sous-cas distinct de M2 qui fait apparaître la nécessité de l'analyse de signe — il ne déclenche pas sma_limit_calc.M1 (la forme n'est pas 0/0).
distinguishing_mcq_stem.correct_rationale: Le numérateur tend vers 3 (non nul) ; le dénominateur (x−1)² tend vers 0 par valeurs strictement positives au voisinage de 1 (carré, donc ≥ 0, et strictement > 0 pour x ≠ 1). Le quotient d'un terme tendant vers 3 par un terme tendant vers 0⁺ tend vers +∞. La technique correcte est l'analyse de signe du dénominateur — étape omise par le modèle erroné qui s'arrête à « 3/0 = indéfini ».

authoring_notes.filter_criteria: Per ADR 0008 §'4-criteria filter'. Each misconception must be (a) a named misunderstanding (wrong model), not a procedural error; (b) contradicted by a named principle in contradicts_principle; (c) distinguishable from every other misconception in this set via at least one MCQ stem only it would lead a student to answer incorrectly; (d) supported by named math-education literature, the Moroccan SM-A cadre de référence, or a Bac-paper year/session citation. 'Common student error' alone fails (d).

candidates_cut.summary: « Le théorème de comparaison (gendarmes) s'applique même quand les fonctions d'encadrement n'ont pas la même limite »
candidates_cut.filter_result: Fails criterion (c). The diagnostic stem for this misconception (student applies sandwich theorem when upper and lower bounds have different limits) cannot be cleanly distinguished from a procedural error (student made a calculation mistake on one bound). The wrong-answer signature does not uniquely identify the model — it overlaps with arithmetic slips. A wrong model whose only observable is a wrong number fails the distinguishability criterion. Not borderline; cut.

candidates_cut.summary: « La limite d'un produit est nulle si l'un des facteurs tend vers 0, même quand l'autre tend vers ∞ (forme 0·∞) »
candidates_cut.filter_result: The model itself passes all four criteria (a)-(d) and is strongly supported. Cut from v1 because the natural diagnostic stem (lim(x→0⁺) x·ln(x)) has correct answer = 0, which is ALSO the answer predicted by the misconception. This is the ADR 0012 cross-contamination failure mode applied to the correct answer: the item cannot distinguish a correctly-reasoning student from a misconception-holding student. Suitable stems exist (e.g., lim(x→0⁺) x·(1/x²) = +∞, where the misconception predicts 0 and the correct answer is +∞) but require more careful cadre-fit validation before ship. Deferred to v2 authoring — the model and the evidence record are preserved here so v2 starts with a prepared candidate.
candidates_cut.v2_stem_candidate: lim(x→0⁺) x · (1/x²) = ?  Correct = +∞ (not reachable via M1 or M3 reasoning). Misconception predicts 0 (zero × anything = zero). Correct rationale: x · (1/x²) = 1/x → +∞. Cross-contamination check: M1 doesn't fire (no sum/oscillation); M3 doesn't fire (no explicit fraction with denominator-→-0 form). Candidate passes the v2 check — ship after cadre validation.

authoring_notes.authoring_order_for_teaching: M1 (somme-limites-inexistantes) fires first: students encounter sum-of-limits in the same lesson where the operational theorems are introduced, and the cosine/sine oscillation case is the canonical first confrontation with a sum whose terms individually lack limits. M2 (quotient-denominateur-nul) fires whenever any fraction is evaluated at a point where the denominator vanishes — which is the most frequent non-trivial limit problem in the SM-A cadre (rational functions, trigonometric quotients). The cut candidate produit-zero-infini-est-zero would fire later, after transcendental functions are introduced, and is deferred to v2.
authoring_notes.close_to_the_line:
M1 (somme-limites-inexistantes) on the stem lim(x→+∞) (x + cos x): distractor A ('la limite n'existe pas car lim cos(x) n'existe pas') is the primary M1 signature. Distractor D ('+∞ + lim cos(x), ce qui est indéfini') is a softer-framed variant of the same wrong model — the student decomposes the sum AND attempts to invoke the additive theorem on a non-existent term, surfaces the impossibility, but still concludes indéterminé rather than reaching for the comparison theorem. Step 3 (item authoring) should dual-tag A (primary) + D (secondary) on M1-targeting items, mirroring slice 1's M1 (B+C) and M4 (C+B) dual-tagging patterns.

M2 (quotient-denominateur-nul) on the revised 1/0 stem lim(x→1) (x+2)/(x−1)²: distractor B ('la limite n'existe pas car on divise par 0') is the primary signature — the M2-holder who omits sign analysis and stops at 'c/0 is undefined' lands here. The other plausible M2 signature ('+∞ sans analyse de signe' — the M2-holder who treats c/0 as ∞ without sign analysis) coincides with the correct answer A on this stem. Step 3 should NOT dual-tag A as a secondary M2 marker on this item: doing so would tag the right-answer reasoner. Right-reason vs wrong-reason students who both arrive at A are diagnostically indistinguishable on this item; resolving them requires a different stem (e.g., a 1/0 form where the sign analysis flips the sign — lim(x→1) (x−4)/(x−1)² where correct = −∞ and the mechanical M2-holder says '+∞' or 'doesn't exist'). This is a step-3-design note, not a defect in the seed.
authoring_notes.v2_stem_design_check:
Per ADR 0012 §'Pedagogy-auditor: cross-contamination matrix' AND the across-skill expansion (forthcoming ADR 0014, originated by slice 2's M2 stem revision — see pedagogy-auditor.md Hard Rules): for each shipped misconception, the correct answer and the target distractor must NOT be reachable via reasoning consistent with any non-target misconception in the current skill's set OR any misconception in the sets of adjacent skills the student plausibly holds state on. 'Adjacent' = same matière + same unité, plus one-hop on the prerequisite DAG. For sma_limit_ops, the adjacent set includes sma_limit_calc (same unité 'Limites et continuité', same matière 'math'); verification walks sma_limit_calc's four misconceptions M1 (forme-indeterminee-valeur-nulle), M2 (limite-egale-valeur-point), M3 (infini-moins-infini-nul), M4 (limite-fondamentale-linearite) in addition to the within-skill set.

M1 (somme-limites-inexistantes) — stem: lim(x→+∞) (x + cos x), correct = +∞ (choice B), target distractor = 'la limite n'existe pas' (choice A).
  WITHIN-SKILL:
  - Can M2-reasoning (quotient-denominateur-nul) reach A or B? No fraction present — no denominator to evaluate. M2 does not fire. Not contaminated.
  - Can cut-candidate produit-zero-infini reasoning reach A or B? No product of a zero-tending and an infinity-tending term visible. The sum form does not trigger that model. Not contaminated.
  ACROSS-SKILL (sma_limit_calc):
  - sma_limit_calc.M1 (forme-indeterminee-valeur-nulle, 0/0): the stem is a sum at +∞, not a quotient at a finite point with 0/0 form. M1 specifically fires on substitution-yields-0/0 cases. Does not fire on +∞ + bounded oscillation. Not contaminated.
  - sma_limit_calc.M2 (limite-egale-valeur-point, 'lim_a f = f(a)'): the limit is at +∞, not at a finite point. M2's substitution behavior is undefined at infinity — no value to plug in. Does not fire. Not contaminated.
  - sma_limit_calc.M3 (infini-moins-infini-nul, '∞ − ∞ = 0'): M3 requires recognition of an explicit subtraction-of-infinities form. The stem is x + cos(x): one term tends to +∞, the other oscillates bounded between −1 and +1. A student does not naturally parse this as '∞ − ∞'. Could a student misread cos(x) as 'tending to a value that subtracts off +∞'? Unlikely — that's not M3's signature reasoning, which is specifically about polynomial/radical forms like x²−x or √(x²+1)−x. Not a clean signature reach. Not contaminated.
  - sma_limit_calc.M4 (limite-fondamentale-linearite, 'sin(ax)/x = a'): requires a trigonometric fundamental form sin(u)/u with u→0. The stem has cos at +∞, not sin at 0. Form mismatch. Does not fire. Not contaminated.
  Verdict: A and B are not reachable via any non-M1 model in either the within-skill set or the adjacent-skill set. PASS.

M2 (quotient-denominateur-nul) — stem: lim(x→1) (x+2)/(x−1)², correct = +∞ (choice A), target distractor = 'la limite n'existe pas car on divise par 0' (choice B). REVISED FROM 0/0 FORM TO 1/0 FORM — see ADR 0014 (forthcoming) and pedagogy-auditor.md Hard Rules for the originating finding.
  WITHIN-SKILL:
  - Can M1-reasoning (somme-limites-inexistantes) reach A or B? M1 concerns decomposing a sum where an individual term lacks a limit (oscillation case). The stem is a quotient at a finite point, not a sum at infinity. M1 does not naturally parse this stem and does not produce a specific numerical conclusion. Not contaminated.
  - Can cut-candidate produit-zero-infini reasoning reach A or B? The expression is a quotient, not a product. The cut model fires when a student sees an explicit f·g with f→0 and g→∞. No such product visible. Not contaminated.
  ACROSS-SKILL (sma_limit_calc):
  - sma_limit_calc.M1 (forme-indeterminee-valeur-nulle, 0/0): THIS IS THE TARGETED EXCLUSION. At x=1, numerator → 3 (non-zero), denominator → 0. The form is 3/0, NOT 0/0. M1's signature reasoning ('substitution yields 0/0 → conclude 0 or doesn't exist or 1') requires a 0/0 form to fire. The 1/0 form does not match M1's trigger pattern. M1 does not fire on this stem — the entire point of the revision from the prior 0/0 stem. Not contaminated.
  - sma_limit_calc.M2 (limite-egale-valeur-point, 'lim_a f = f(a)'): at x=1, f(1) = 3/0 is undefined — the function is not defined at the target point. M2's signature is 'substitute a, return f(a)'. With f(1) undefined, M2's reasoning has no clean output: the M2-holder either concludes 'f isn't defined here, I don't know' (no diagnostic output, not a reach on A or B) or shifts to a different model. M2 does not deterministically reach A=+∞ or B='doesn't exist' via its signature reasoning path. (Note: a student might bridge from M2's confusion to a generic 'limit must not exist' conclusion, which could land on B — but that's not M2's signature reach; it's a model shift toward sma_limit_ops.M2 itself. Not contaminated by M2 alone.) Not contaminated.
  - sma_limit_calc.M3 (infini-moins-infini-nul, '∞ − ∞ = 0'): no subtraction of infinities present. The stem is a quotient at a finite point. Form mismatch. Does not fire. Not contaminated.
  - sma_limit_calc.M4 (limite-fondamentale-linearite, 'sin(ax)/x = a'): no trig fundamental form. Does not fire. Not contaminated.
  Verdict: A=+∞ and B='doesn't exist' are not reachable via any non-M2 model in either the within-skill set or the adjacent-skill set. PASS.

Cut candidate (produit-zero-infini-est-zero) — no stem shipped. The cut was forced precisely by a correct-answer collision: on the natural stem lim(x→0⁺) x·ln(x), the misconception predicts 0 and the correct answer IS 0. Item cannot distinguish. The v2_stem_candidate in candidates_cut proposes lim(x→0⁺) x·(1/x²) where correct = +∞ and misconception predicts 0 — no collision on the within-skill axis. The across-skill axis was not re-walked for this candidate in slice 2; ship-time check (v2 authoring) must repeat the expanded walk against sma_limit_calc M1-M4.

Summary: both shipped stems pass the correct-answer-and-target-distractor cross-contamination check on BOTH the within-skill axis and the across-skill axis (sma_limit_calc). The prior M2 stem (0/0 form) failed the across-skill check post-hoc; its replacement (1/0 form) was selected precisely to evade sma_limit_calc.M1's 0/0 trigger pattern. The cut candidate's collision is documented and its v2 stem requires the expanded walk before ship.
